title: Call If You Need Me: The Uncollected Fiction And Prose Of Raymond Carver
pull_quote: Raymond Carver divided his life into two parts - Bad Raymond, the drinking  years, and Good Raymond, the later years, many of which he spent looking  back, thinking how his past might have worked out otherwise. As a writer, his  output was fairly small, and the stories themselves are spare - honed down to a  lean perfection. It seemed that everything he had written was in the public  domain, mulled over, cherished. Then, following his death in 1988, a few more discoveries were made. The story we publish here, in a world exclusive, What  Would You Like To See?, is the last of the last. Carver wrote it, probably in the  early to mid 80s, and it harks back to 1977, the year when he was on the cusp of turning from 'Bad' to 'Good'. Soon after, he sold it, unheralded, with a batch of other documents to a university library - maybe because he  needed the money.
headline: What Would You Like To See?
